{   "summary": "General situation: The global grains and oilseeds markets remain stable with no significant price movements or fundamental shifts observed in the past week. Brazilian corn and soybeans prices held steady around 112.7 USD/MT and 662.9 USD/MT respectively, while US spot prices for corn and soybeans remained near 394.5 USD/MT. What changed vs previous comparable period: There was no notable change in market dynamics or pricing compared to the prior week, with no new impactful news or shifts in supply-demand fundamentals. However, freight market disruptions are increasingly common, as noted by recent tanker market volatility, which could affect export logistics. Actionable implications for trading/brokerage: Traders should monitor freight cost spikes and potential export delays, especially for corn shipments from European ports like Tarragona, where offers are currently around 241 EUR/MT for April delivery. Sunflower bids in Marmara at 301 USD/MT indicate steady demand in the vegetable oilseed segment. Maintaining flexible logistics strategies and watching freight market developments will be key to managing risk. 

Key facts:
- Brazilian corn FOB Santos price at 112.7 USD/MT as of March 12, 2026
- Brazilian soybeans price steady at 662.9 USD/MT as of March 14, 2026
- US spot corn and soybeans prices stable at 394.5 USD/MT as of February 4, 2026
- Argentine barley Grade 2 Up River priced at 212 USD/MT for December 2025 delivery
- Freight offers for corn CIF Tarragona at 241 EUR/MT for April 10-30 shipments
- Sunflower bids CPT Marmara at 301 USD/MT for first half of March shipments
